messages.subject: DSM data file structure + pantropical dolphins (dsm example analysis) package dependencies archived
parts:
Hello Distance list serve champions,

I am setting up my flatfile data frames for a dsm and have a couple questions regarding the data structure. Although I looked at both the dsm-data help page in R and also through previous posts in this group and need a tiny bit of clarity. I have reviewed the pantropical dolphins dsm example and will use the same data frame titles for reference.
Question 1:
When structuring my distance data (referred to as "distdata" in the dolphins dsm example), do I include transect lines where no observations occurred with an "NA" (or nothing entered) under the distance + size columns?
According to post+response in this group from Oct. 2019, titled "Data structure for DSM", it seems that the answer is NO, but according to both the 2019 Miller et al paper (Distance Sampling in R) and also the response in this group from March 2023 titled "No observations on a transect" for line transect distance sampling, the answer is YES, include transect lines which had no observations and leave both the "size" column and "distance" column blank (or with NA).
Question 2:
When structuring the same "distdata" to run the detection function, do I use the full transect length for the column "Effort" where the "Sample.Label" has the unique transect line name, then use the "obsdata" data frame and link the Sample.Label (unique transect ID from distdata) with the Segment.Label (from segsdata)? If this is how the obsdata data frame should be structured, do I also include the transects that did not have any animal observations?
Question3:
When trying to run the pantropical dolphins example, I am unable to install or load 2 packages: maptools and rgdal. Is there a workaround for these packages being archived? I'm using R version 4.4.1.

Thanks for your time and for this resource!

--
Kat Bernier
Ph.D. Candidate
University of California, Santa Cruz

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM data file structure + pantropical dolphins (dsm example analysis) package dependencies archived
parts:
Kat

Thanks for doing such thorough homework prior to sending your questions to the list. That is why past messages are available to search. Let me address your questions in order:
  1. NAs in distdata file. When constructing data files for dsm this is done differently then when organising data for the Distance package. As the distdata name suggests, this data frame contains information about the detection distances. Consequently, it will not contain information about transects without detections.
  2. Staying with the distdata data frame, the Effort column in this data frame will be the length of the transect. The same holds true for the obsdata data frame; Effort is transect length. That is not true for the segdata data frame; Effort there is segment length. obsdata contains information only about observations; therefore there will be no NAs for distance or size.
  3. You are correct that the pantropical dolphin example as presented in our examples vignette depends upon depreciated packages.
    1. we are in the process of updating our examples (more information about that in a month or two). Meanwhile, you can have a glimpse in advance of the pantropical dolphin analysis with those dependencies removed here:
      1. http://distancedevelopment.github.io/dsm/articles/lines_gomex/mexico-analysis.html
Hope that clears up the ambiguity.
